queries: WITH per_patient AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS igg, AVG(e.ANA) AS ana FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), per_sex AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(igg) AS avg_igg, AVG(ana) AS avg_ana FROM per_patient GROUP BY SEX) SELECT SEX, avg_igg AS avg_aCL_IgG, avg_ana AS avg_ANA, avg_ana / (SELECT AVG(avg_ana) FROM per_sex) AS ana_ratio_to_mean_of_sex_avgs FROM per_sex

WITH per_patient AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS igg, AVG(e.ANA) AS ana FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND p.SEX <> '' GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), per_sex AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(igg) AS avg_igg, AVG(ana) AS avg_ana FROM per_patient GROUP BY SEX) SELECT SEX, avg_igg AS avg_aCL_IgG, avg_ana AS avg_ANA, avg_ana / (SELECT AVG(avg_ana) FROM per_sex) AS ana_ratio_to_mean_of_sex_avgs FROM per_sex

assumptions.assumption: Patients with a NULL or empty SEX are kept as their own group (NULL sex) and that group counts in the mean of per-sex average ANA values.
The mean of the per-sex average ANA values is the unweighted mean across sex groups that have a non-null average ANA. Groups whose ANA is entirely missing are ignored in that mean.
A patient whose examinations all have a NULL aCL IgG (or ANA) contributes nothing to that average but still counts for the other measure.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude patients with a NULL or empty SEX, so only real sex groups appear and enter the mean of per-sex averages.
alternatives.sql: WITH per_patient AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS igg, AVG(e.ANA) AS ana FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND p.SEX <> '' GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), per_sex AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(igg) AS avg_igg, AVG(ana) AS avg_ana FROM per_patient GROUP BY SEX) SELECT SEX, avg_igg AS avg_aCL_IgG, avg_ana AS avg_ANA, avg_ana / (SELECT AVG(avg_ana) FROM per_sex) AS ana_ratio_to_mean_of_sex_avgs FROM per_sex

assumptions.assumption: The 'mean of the per-sex average ANA values' is the unweighted mean across sexes, taken over the sex groups shown, including any NULL/blank sex group if present. A sex group whose average ANA is NULL is excluded from that mean by AVG.
Each patient's average is computed over only their non-null values, so a patient with no ANA is ignored in the ANA average but can still count in the aCL IgG average.

responses.sql: WITH per_patient AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(e.`aCL IgG`) AS igg, AVG(e.ANA) AS ana FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), per_sex AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(igg) AS avg_igg, AVG(ana) AS avg_ana FROM per_patient GROUP BY SEX) SELECT SEX, avg_igg AS avg_aCL_IgG, avg_ana AS avg_ANA, avg_ana / (SELECT AVG(avg_ana) FROM per_sex) AS ana_ratio_to_mean_of_sex_averages FROM per_sex

assumptions.assumption: Patients with a NULL or empty SEX value are kept as their own group (NULL group) and included in the mean of per-sex ANA averages; the mean is taken over all groups returned.
The ratio's denominator is the unweighted mean of the per-sex average ANA values (each sex counts once), as stated in the request.
A patient whose examinations all have NULL aCL IgG or ANA yields NULL for that measure and is ignored in that measure's sex average.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude patients with NULL SEX from the output and from the mean of per-sex averages.
